summary: On the eighth day Jesus is circumcised as the law requires and receives the name Jesus, the name the angel gave before He was conceived.
key_insight: The first rite performed on Jesus was the covenant sign given to Abraham, and the name He received means the LORD saves. From His eighth day the Savior was placed under the law He came to fulfill, “born under the law” (Galatians 4:4).
story: When eight days had passed, the time came for the Child to be circumcised, as the law of Moses required for every Jewish boy.
On that day He received His name. “His name was called JESUS, the name given by the angel before He was conceived in the womb.”
The family did not choose the name. Months earlier, before Mary was with child, the angel Gabriel had told her what to call her Son, and now the Child was given that name and no other.

scene.label: The eighth day
scene.text: God gave circumcision to Abraham as the sign of His covenant, to be done on the eighth day (Genesis 17:9–12; Leviticus 12:3). Every Jewish boy, Jesus included, was marked in this way as a member of the covenant people.

scene.label: Named at circumcision
scene.text: As with John (Luke 1:59–63), the name was given at the circumcision. Matthew adds that Joseph “called His name JESUS” (Matthew 1:25), acting as the Child’s legal father.

scene.label: The name
scene.text: Jesus is the Greek form of Yeshua, a later form of Joshua, meaning the LORD saves. It was a common name; Paul mentions a fellow worker, “Jesus who is called Justus” (Colossians 4:11). What set this Child’s name apart was who gave it and why (Matthew 1:21).

scene.label: Where
scene.text: Luke does not say where the circumcision took place. Since the family was still near Jerusalem several weeks later (Luke 2:22), it was probably in Bethlehem.

witnesses.luke: Only Luke records the circumcision and naming, in a single verse. He shows Jesus’ parents keeping the law at each step after His birth: circumcision, then purification and presentation in the temple (Luke 2:22–24). The verse also completes Gabriel’s word to Mary in Luke 1:31.

seeing.reveals: Jesus belonged fully to His people. He bore the covenant sign in His own body and carried a name that announced His mission: the LORD saves.
seeing.living: The name Jesus was God’s choice, given before He was conceived. When you pray in Jesus’ name, you call on the name God Himself chose, “the name which is above every name” (Philippians 2:9). It is not a formula to close a prayer; it is the ground of every request.
seeing.ponder: When you say the name Jesus, do you hear in it the promise that the LORD saves, and that He saves you?

preaching.big_idea: God named His Son Jesus and placed Him under the law to redeem those under it.
outline: Under the law from the eighth day (21a)
A promise kept to the letter (21c)
preaching.watch_for: Compare John’s naming, told in six verses full of drama (1:59–64), with Jesus’ naming, told in one quiet verse. Luke lets the angel’s earlier word (1:31) carry the weight: God named Him, and His parents simply obeyed.
